n2d8cc2d5e26.s: China occupies about how much Indian territory in Aksai Chin?
n2d8cc2d5e26.x: China occupies about 38,000 sq km in Aksai Chin; the ~90,000 sq km figure is its claim in the north-east (most of Arunachal Pradesh).

n400eeed2dba.s: The India-China war of 1962 (20 October-21 November) ended with:
n400eeed2dba.x: The war ended in China's unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962, not a negotiated one.

n92c75f794b0.s: Which report (1963) reviewed India's military failure in the 1962 war with China?
n92c75f794b0.x: The Henderson Brooks-Bhagat Report (1963) reviewed India's military failure in 1962.

n90af2ffd53d.s: The India-China Border Defence Cooperation Agreement was signed in:
n90af2ffd53d.x: The BDCA was signed in 2013; 2005 was the Political Parameters agreement, 2012 the WMCC and 2003 the Special Representatives.

n733198a945a.s: The 25th round of India-China Special Representatives' talks (August 2026), which issued an eight-point document on the LAC, was held in:
n733198a945a.x: The 25th round was held in Beijing; the 24th round (August 2025) was held in New Delhi.

n79789e6ddbe.s: How many Indian soldiers were killed in the Galwan Valley clash in Eastern Ladakh on 15 June 2020?
n79789e6ddbe.x: Twenty Indian soldiers were killed in the Galwan clash of 15 June 2020 in Eastern Ladakh.

n9132c9243dc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about disengagement at LAC friction points?
o: Gogra-Hot Springs disengagement took place in 2020
Pangong Tso north and south banks disengagement took place in 2021
Depsang and Demchok came under the October 2024 understanding
Galwan was among the disengagement points
n9132c9243dc.x: Gogra-Hot Springs disengagement took place in 2022, not 2020; the other statements are correct.

n9ce5c4f13ee.s: The Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 provided for provincial councils through which amendment of Sri Lanka's Constitution?
n9ce5c4f13ee.x: The 1987 Accord provided for provincial councils through the 13th Amendment, along with the merger of the Northern and Eastern provinces and the IPKF.

n195d5ea3432.s: Under the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement, implemented in 2015, how many Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh?
n195d5ea3432.x: 111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves came to India.

n0dd0bb50b43.s: Who was the first President of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal?
n0dd0bb50b43.x: Ram Baran Yadav was the first President; Prachanda was the first Prime Minister.

n44cf4addfbf.s: Myanmar's military coup of 1 February 2021 was led by:
n44cf4addfbf.x: The coup of 1 February 2021 brought the junta of Senior General Min Aung Hlaing to power; India engages it for Act East and north-east security.

n8efe5772db7.s: In which year did Sri Lanka crush the LTTE?
n8efe5772db7.x: Sri Lanka crushed the LTTE in 2009; it had killed Rajiv Gandhi in 1991 and India banned it in 1992.

n60665b6cf2a.s: Countering China's influence, access to new markets and instability in West and Central Asia were drivers of India's:
n60665b6cf2a.x: All three were drivers of the Look East Policy (a match pair cannot be built honestly from these facts, so a one-liner).

na80dd6e1bb8.s: In 2026, what did the USA do with India's sanctions waiver for Chabahar port?
na80dd6e1bb8.x: In 2026 the USA ended, not extended, India's Chabahar waiver; Chabahar gives India access to Afghanistan, Central Asia and the INSTC bypassing Pakistan.

n0d014d5fc07.s: The fourth C added to the Commerce, Culture and Connectivity framework of the Act East Policy is:
n0d014d5fc07.x: The 4th C is Capacity building, not Climate action.

nf0131ab79ff.s: The Akhaura-Agartala railway link is associated with India and:
nf0131ab79ff.x: Akhaura-Agartala is a rail link with Bangladesh, not an ASEAN-linked project like Kaladan and the Trilateral Highway.

new.s: Which boundary line represents India's claim over Aksai Chin?
new.x: The Johnson Line (1865) put Aksai Chin in Ladakh, India's claim; the Macartney-MacDonald Line placed it under China.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Arunachal Pradesh in India-China relations:
1. China claims about 90,000 sq km in the north-east, most of it in Arunachal.
2. China denied visas to Arunachal members of India's delegation in 1995.
3. The USA has reaffirmed Arunachal as part of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: China claims ~90,000 sq km ('South Tibet'), denied visas in 1995 (Beijing women's conference), and the USA reaffirmed Arunachal as Indian.

new.s: The Middle sector of the LAC, the least contested, covers:
new.x: The Middle sector covers Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand; Ladakh is the Western and Sikkim-Arunachal the Eastern sector.

new.s: The 1962 India-China war was fought in which two sectors?
new.x: The war was fought in Aksai Chin (west) and NEFA (east).

new.s: The Dalai Lama's asylum in India, a cause of the 1962 war, was granted in:
new.x: The Dalai Lama got asylum in India in 1959, one of the causes of the 1962 war.

new.s: The Special Representatives mechanism for India-China boundary talks was set up in 2003 under PM:
new.x: The SR mechanism dates to 2003 (Vajpayee); the 1993 Peace and Tranquillity agreement was under Narasimha Rao.

new.s: The India-China Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC), set up in 2012, deals with:
new.x: The WMCC (2012) handles border affairs, not settlement; settlement talks are with the Special Representatives (2003).

new.s: Which of the following standoff-place pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Sumdorong Chu (1986-87) was in Tawang; Depsang was in Ladakh, Yangtse in Tawang and Doklam at the India-Bhutan-China tri-junction.

new.s: The Yangtse clash in Tawang between Indian and Chinese troops took place on:
new.x: The Yangtse clash in Tawang was on 9 December 2022; 15 June 2020 was Galwan.

new.s: India's trade deficit with China (July 2026) is about:
new.x: The trade deficit with China is about $100 billion, with dependence on machinery, APIs, electronics and solar.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India-China economic ties?
o: The 2020 app bans were made under Section 69A of the IT Act
The Strategic Economic Dialogue was set up in 2010
Press Note 3 (2020) bans FDI from land-border countries
India depends on China for APIs and solar equipment
new.x: Press Note 3 requires government approval for FDI from land-border countries; it is not a ban.

new.s: India-China anti-terror army exercise 'Hand-in-Hand' was first held in 2007 at:
new.x: Hand-in-Hand, the India-China anti-terror army exercise, was first held in 2007 at Kunming.

new.s: Which of the following China-Pakistan exercise-service pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Shaheen is the air force exercise; Warrior is the army and Sea Guardian the navy exercise.

new.s: Which of the following port-country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: Chittagong is in Bangladesh, not Myanmar; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: India and China set up the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers in:
new.x: The Expert Level Mechanism dates to 2006; flood-season data MoUs cover the Brahmaputra and Sutlej.

new.s: The 18th BRICS Summit (September 2026) was held in:
new.x: The 18th BRICS Summit was held in New Delhi in September 2026.

new.s: India's Friendship Treaty with Bhutan was originally signed in:
new.x: The India-Bhutan Friendship Treaty dates to 1949 (revised 2007); the Nepal treaty is of 1950.

new.s: The Tin Bigha corridor was leased to Bangladesh in 1992 for access to:
new.x: Tin Bigha was leased in 1992 to give Bangladesh access to the Dahagram-Angarpota enclaves.

new.s: The Mahakali Treaty of 1996 was signed between India and:
new.x: The Mahakali Treaty (Sarada, Tanakpur, Pancheshwar) is with Nepal; the 1996 Ganga Water Treaty is with Bangladesh.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's water agreements with Nepal:
1. The Kosi Agreement was signed in 1954.
2. The Gandak Agreement was signed in 1996.
3. The Mahakali Treaty covers Sarada, Tanakpur and Pancheshwar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Gandak Agreement was signed in 1959, not 1996.

new.s: Nepal's new Constitution was adopted on:
new.x: Nepal adopted its new Constitution on 20 September 2015; the monarchy was abolished on 28 May 2008.

new.s: The Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 was signed by Rajiv Gandhi and:
new.x: The 1987 Accord was signed by Rajiv Gandhi and J.R. Jayewardene.

new.s: The IPKF was withdrawn from Sri Lanka (last troops left 24 March 1990) on the order of PM:
new.x: The IPKF was withdrawn on V.P. Singh's order; the last troops left on 24 March 1990.

new.s: The Greater Male Connectivity project in the Maldives is a:
new.x: Greater Male Connectivity is a bridge-causeway linking Male to nearby islands, not a tunnel.

new.s: The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway begins in India at:
new.x: The Trilateral Highway runs from Moreh in Manipur to Mae Sot in Thailand.

new.s: The 218 km Zaranj-Delaram highway in Afghanistan was built by India's:
new.x: The Zaranj-Delaram highway (218 km) was built by the BRO and links to the Iran border (Chabahar route).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India-backed power projects in Bangladesh:
1. Rooppur is a nuclear power project built by Russia.
2. Maitree at Rampal is a hydroelectric project.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Maitree at Rampal is a thermal power project.

new.s: Under the first trilateral power deal in the region, Nepal supplies electricity to Bangladesh through:
new.x: Nepal supplies power to Bangladesh through the Indian grid, the first trilateral power trade.

new.s: Which Indian Prime Minister visited Kabul in September 1959?
new.x: PM Nehru visited Kabul in September 1959.

new.s: After the Taliban takeover of August 2021, India stationed a technical team in Kabul in:
new.x: India sent a technical team to Kabul in 2022, besides wheat, medicine and vaccine aid.

new.s: Which of the following issue-country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The Doklam tri-junction concerns Bhutan, not Nepal; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: Hambantota port in Sri Lanka is seen as part of India's encirclement by:
new.x: Hambantota is part of the Chinese, not Pakistani, encirclement (APPSC G1 2024).

new.s: India's economic crisis support of about $4 billion in 2022 went to:
new.x: India gave Sri Lanka about $4 billion during its 2022 economic crisis.

new.s: India's Act East Policy was launched in 2014 at the:
new.x: Act East was launched at the East Asia Summit in Myanmar (2014), not at a SAARC Summit.

new.s: India's Look East Policy (1991-92) was launched under Prime Minister:
new.x: Look East was launched under P.V. Narasimha Rao; Act East under Narendra Modi.

new.s: India's Connect Central Asia policy was launched in 2012 at:
new.x: Connect Central Asia was launched at Bishkek in 2012; Samarkand hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue (2019).

new.s: Under the Act East Policy, which region of India is the gateway to ASEAN?
new.x: The North-East is India's gateway to ASEAN under Act East.

new.s: In 2019, the leaders of which grouping were invited to the PM's swearing-in, extending Neighbourhood First?
new.x: SAARC leaders were invited in May 2014; BIMSTEC leaders in 2019.

new.s: The I2U2, called the 'West Asia Quad', comprises India, Israel, the USA and:
new.x: I2U2 is India, Israel, UAE and USA.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's Link West engagement:
1. India's trade with the GCC is over $160 billion.
2. The first I2U2 leaders' summit was held virtually in 2022.
3. I2U2 is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: GCC trade exceeds $160 billion, the first I2U2 summit was virtual (2022) and it is handled by MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.

new.s: SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) was announced in 2015 in:
new.x: SAGAR was announced in Mauritius in 2015; MAHASAGAR was also announced in Mauritius (2025).

new.s: SHANTI, India's framework for shared maritime spaces (13 July 2026), was launched by:
new.x: SHANTI was launched by EAM Jaishankar, not the PM.

new.s: In which year was SAGAR upgraded to MAHASAGAR?
new.x: MAHASAGAR came in 2025 (Mauritius); SAGAR was 2015 and SHANTI 2026.

new.s: How many pillars does the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) have?
new.x: IPOI has seven pillars, from Maritime Security to Trade Connectivity and Maritime Transport.

new.s: The Information Fusion Centre-Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) was inaugurated in December 2018 at:
new.x: IFC-IOR was inaugurated on 22 December 2018 at IMAC, Gurugram, hosted by the Indian Navy.

new.s: The Colombo Security Conclave began in 2011 as a trilateral of India, Sri Lanka and:
new.x: It began as India, Sri Lanka and Maldives; Mauritius, Bangladesh and Seychelles joined later.

new.s: Which of the following island project-country pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: Assumption Island is in Seychelles, not Maldives; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: The Hanimaadhoo airport project is in:
new.x: Hanimaadhoo airport, like the Uthuru Thila Falhu harbour, is in the Maldives.

new.s: The coastal radar chain, IFC-IOR and island projects are flagship initiatives of which doctrine?
new.x: SAGAR (2015) widened into MAHASAGAR and IPOI; its flagships are the radar chain, IFC-IOR and island projects.

new.s: India's Think West doctrine has widened in scope into which grouping?
new.x: Think West (Gulf, Iran, Israel) has widened into I2U2.
